lines.text: For two years, I ran our community's account. One login. Mine.
I could post anything, in everyone's name. And if I left, the account left with me.
And those of us who wrote the posts? We never saw a cent.
Choir is a community account that nobody can log in to.
It's a real NEAR account with no keys. Nobody can make it say anything. It only repeats what its members post. And it pays them.
So I post from my own account, like always. Then I ask the Choir to repeat it.
The account reposts her. Her words, under her name.
A reader sends a tip. It's split the moment it lands: most of it goes to the members who were repeated, and a small, capped cut to the seat.
When the round ends, the account posts its own receipt. Nobody typed that.
And I got paid. For a post!
Then it was time for me to step down. There was no password to hand over. Just the seat.
The seat is an NFT. One transaction, and Sam is the conductor. The account announces it, by itself.
I tried my old desk. It's closed.
Because this account has no keys at all. And anyone can check.
The members keep everything they earned.
And the community keeps its account.
